why: T44 (SA-24): the padded sampling branch never read bond_length_guidance_weight, so pad_groups:on sampled without the term while pad_groups:off sampled with it, silently. T37: the same branch ran without torch.no_grad while the grouped branch had it.
code_change: _BondLengthGuidance gains node_mask; radius_edge_index is called with it instead of None
trainer: _with_bond_length_guidance() is now the ONE place the wrapper is built; both branches call it
the padded loop body is wrapped in torch.no_grad()

padding_does_not_leak.setup: 6 real atoms + 3 padding atoms placed INSIDE the cutoff of the real ones
padding_does_not_leak.measured: real-atom guidance force identical with and without the padding present (atol 1e-6); padding atoms receive exactly zero

red_check.method: temporarily reverted each fix and re-ran the file

honest_limits: The equivalence is measured at the VELOCITY level on the real atoms, not as an end-to-end coordinate comparison. The two paths draw their noise from torch.randn calls of different shapes, so a coordinate comparison needs an injected x0 the sampler does not expose.

test_cfm_pad_groups_equivalence.py's docstring claimed it compared generated coordinates between the two paths; it never did. The claim is corrected in that file and the gap is recorded here rather than closed.
No GPU run. The no_grad change reduces peak memory but no number here quantifies by how much.
